extractions.value: Initial presentation was atypical for classic SPS, with asymmetric limb involvement and slowness mimicking Parkinsonism. The patient was initially misdiagnosed as a young-onset Parkinsonian disorder and treated with levodopa without benefit. Later developed myoclonus, encephalopathy, and worsening rigidity reminiscent of PERM, but it was unclear if this was related to COVID-19 infection, GAD65, or an alternative undiagnosed cause. The patient died 46 months after presentation.
extractions.quote: This case's initial presentation represents a deviation from classic stiffperson syndrome. ... While this case did have myoclonus, encephalopathy, and worsening of her muscle rigidity, reminiscent of PERM, it was not clear if her syndrome was related to her COVID19 infection, GAD65 or an alternative undiagnosed cause.
